sentences.en: When you come back to England from any foreign country, you have immediately the sensation of breathing a different air.
sentences.zh: 当你从任何外国回到英国，你会立刻有一种呼吸到不同空气的感觉。

sentences.en: Even in the first few minutes, dozens of small things conspire to give you this feeling.
sentences.zh: 即使是在最初的几分钟里，无数细微的事物都在共同营造这种感觉。

sentences.en: The beer is bitterer, the coins are heavier, the grass is greener, the advertisements are more blatant.
sentences.zh: 啤酒更苦，硬币更重，草地更绿，广告也更刺眼。

sentences.en: The crowds in the big towns with their mild, knobby faces, their bad teeth and gentle manners are different from a European crowd.
sentences.zh: 大城镇里的人群，有着温和而棱角分明的面孔、糟糕的牙齿和文雅的举止，与欧洲的人群截然不同。

sentences.en: Then the vastness of England swallows you up and you lose for a while your feeling that the whole nation has a single identifiable character.
sentences.zh: 随后，英国的广袤将你吞没，你暂时失去了那种认为整个国家拥有单一可辨识性格的感觉。

sentences.en: Are there really such things as nations?
sentences.zh: 真的存在“国家”这种东西吗？

sentences.en: Are we not 46 million individuals or different?
sentences.zh: 我们难道不是四千六百万个个体，或者说各不相同吗？

sentences.en: And the diversity of it, the chaos, the clatter of clogs in the Lancashire mill towns, the to and fro of the lorries on the Great North Road,
sentences.zh: 还有它的多样性、混乱，兰开夏郡磨坊镇里木屐的咔哒声，大北路上卡车来来往往的喧嚣，

sentences.en: the queues outside the labour exchanges, the rattle of pin tables in the Soho pubs, the old maids hiking to Holy Communion through the mists of the autumn morning.
sentences.zh: 劳工介绍所外排起的长队，苏豪区酒吧里弹球机的响声，秋日清晨薄雾中徒步去领圣餐的老处女们。

sentences.en: All these are not only fragments, but characteristic fragments of the English scene.
sentences.zh: 所有这些不仅是碎片，更是英国景象中极具代表性的碎片。

sentences.en: How can one make a pattern out of this muddle?
sentences.zh: 怎么能从这团混乱中理出头绪呢？

sentences.en: So Tom Holland, that was friend of the show, George Orwell, writing during the Blitz.
sentences.zh: 所以汤姆·霍兰，那是我们节目的老朋友乔治·奥威尔，写于闪电战期间。

sentences.en: Probably the single most famous evocation of England and Englishness ever written.
sentences.zh: 这可能是史上最著名的对英国和英国性的描绘。

sentences.en: And it strikes me that every single element of it is now utterly out of date.
sentences.zh: 我突然意识到，其中的每一个元素现在都已经彻底过时了。

sentences.en: Do you think that's fair?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这样说公平吗？

sentences.en: I think that's a bit harsh because he's talking about the diversity of England.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这有点苛刻，因为他谈论的是英国的多样性。

sentences.en: And if anything, England's become, I mean, clearly become infinitely more diverse than when Orwell was writing about it.
sentences.zh: 而且如果说有什么变化的话，我的意思是，英国显然变得比奥威尔写作时要多元得多。

sentences.en: But yeah, I think there is still a sense of what, I mean, England still has a place in the imagination of those who live in the country that is called England.
sentences.zh: 但确实，我认为在那些生活在这个被称为英国的国家的人们的想象中，英国仍然占有一席之地。

sentences.en: So to that extent, I think he is onto something.
sentences.zh: 所以从这个程度上来说，我认为他抓住了重点。

sentences.en: I mean, obviously, all the stuff about old maids cycling to Communion and the clatter of clogs on Lancashire streets, I mean, that's gone.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，很明显，那些关于老处女骑车去领圣餐、兰开夏郡街道上木屐的咔哒声，这些都已经消失了。

sentences.en: But plus ça change, c'est la même chose, as Orwell would doubtless have put it.
sentences.zh: 但正如奥威尔无疑会说的那样，Plus ça change, c'est la même chose（变化越多，本质越同）。

sentences.en: He would definitely not have.
sentences.zh: 他绝对不会那么说。

sentences.en: There was no way he would have put that.
sentences.zh: 他绝不可能那样表达。

sentences.en: I mean, basically, are there continuities from the present through to the mid-20th century, when Orwell was writing that, that go further back or not?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从根本上讲，从现在到奥威尔写作的20世纪中叶，是否存在某种延续性，或者说这种延续性是否追溯得更久远？

sentences.en: I mean, great question.
sentences.zh: 这是个好问题。

sentences.en: Well, it's a question about all nations.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个关于所有国家的问题。

sentences.en: But what makes it particularly interesting about England is that England is one of the most famous examples of a nation that is not a nation state.
sentences.zh: 但英国之所以特别有趣，是因为它是最著名的“非民族国家”的例子之一。

sentences.en: So, you know, England has no seat at the United Nations General Assembly.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，英国在联合国大会上没有席位。

sentences.en: A lot of people who live in England do not describe themselves as English.
sentences.zh: 许多住在英国的人并不称自己为英国人。

sentences.en: They say they're British.
sentences.zh: 他们说自己是英国人（不列颠人）。

sentences.en: But abroad, of course, everybody typically confuses England and Britain, as we often do ourselves, don't we?
sentences.zh: 但在国外，当然，每个人通常都会混淆英格兰和英国，就像我们自己也经常混淆一样，不是吗？

sentences.en: I think less so, though.
sentences.zh: 不过我觉得现在少多了。

sentences.en: So I think that's another feature, is that the sense the English have of themselves within a nation called the United Kingdom has definitely grown over the past decade.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这是另一个特征，即英国人在“联合王国”这个国家内对自身身份的认同感在过去十年里确实增强了。

sentences.en: It has indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: I would say.
sentences.zh: 我是这么认为的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so somebody who's been a great observer at this, Tom, or are you going to introduce him?
sentences.zh: 那么，汤姆，作为对此有深刻观察的人，你要介绍他吗？

sentences.en: Because you, I believe, have played cricket with him, I guess.
sentences.zh: 因为我相信你曾和他一起打过板球，我猜。

sentences.en: I have.
sentences.zh: 我打过。

sentences.en: So few things are more archetypally English than a game of cricket on a summer green.
sentences.zh: 没有什么比在夏日的草坪上打一场板球更具典型的英国特色了。

sentences.en: And I played cricket with Jason on one of the most famous days in recent English history, which was the day of the death of Princess Diana.
sentences.zh: 我和杰森在英国近代史上最著名的一天打过板球，那就是戴安娜王妃去世的那一天。

sentences.en: And the game went ahead, but in a rather embarrassed way.
sentences.zh: 比赛照常进行了，但气氛相当尴尬。

sentences.en: So I remember we lined up outside the pavilion, which had a flagpole.
sentences.zh: 我记得我们排队站在凉亭外，那里有一根旗杆。

sentences.en: And the flagpole was at half maSt.
sentences.zh: 旗杆降了半旗。

sentences.en: And we all stood there.
sentences.zh: 我们都站在那里。

sentences.en: We didn't really know what to do.
sentences.zh: 我们真的不知道该做什么。

sentences.en: So we took our caps off and twisted them in an embarrassed way, put them on, and then we just kind of shuffled off,
sentences.zh: 于是我们摘下帽子，尴尬地扭动着，又戴上，然后就那样挪开了，

sentences.en: which I thought was a – I think Orwell would probably have recognised the quality of embarrassment there.
sentences.zh: 我想——我觉得奥威尔大概能体会到那种尴尬的特质。

sentences.en: But am I not also right in thinking that you had a very – you were ferociously upbraided by your captain in the course of this match?
sentences.zh: 但我没记错的话，你在那场比赛中还被你的队长严厉训斥过，对吧？

sentences.en: So we then went on to play the match, and the captain – We haven't even let him speak yet.
sentences.zh: 我们接着进行了比赛，队长——我们还没让他开口呢。

sentences.en: We haven't even introduced him.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至还没介绍他。

sentences.en: The captain, who for now will remain nameless.
sentences.zh: 那位队长，暂时先不提他的名字。

sentences.en: His idea of man management was, as I was bowling, to yell at me, you're losing us for match!
sentences.zh: 他管理人员的理念就是，在我投球时对我大吼：“你快把我们比赛搞砸了！”

sentences.en: And the more tense I got, the more abusive he became.
sentences.zh: 我越紧张，他骂得越凶。

sentences.en: And I knew then that he was destined for a great thing.
sentences.zh: 那时我就知道他注定要成就一番大事业。

sentences.en: And sure enough, he went on to edit The New Statesman, displaying his ability for leadership.
sentences.zh: 果然，他后来去编辑《新政治家》杂志，展现了他的领导才能。

sentences.en: And it is, of course, the great Jason Cowley, one of the great editors of our age, being at the helm of The New Statesman for how long now, Jason?
sentences.zh: 当然，他就是伟大的杰森·考利，我们这个时代最伟大的编辑之一，掌舵《新政治家》多久了，杰森？

sentences.en: 20 years?
It feels like 20 years.
sentences.zh: 感觉像20年了。

sentences.en: 13, Tom.
sentences.zh: 13年，汤姆。

sentences.en: 13 years.
And before that, you were a great sports journalist at the helm of The Observer Sports Weekly when they had that.
sentences.zh: 在那之前，你是《观察家体育周刊》的杰出体育记者，当时他们还有那份刊物。

sentences.en: Yeah, it was monthly.
sentences.zh: 是的，那是月刊。

sentences.en: Oh, it was a monthly, was it?
sentences.zh: 哦，是月刊吗？

sentences.en: And then I edited Granta for a year, a literary quarterly.
sentences.zh: 后来我编辑了《格兰塔》杂志一年，那是一份文学季刊。

sentences.en: So Jason, finger on the absolute pulse of English and dare one say British culture.
sentences.zh: 所以杰森，你绝对是英国文化，甚至可以说是不列颠文化的脉搏所在。

sentences.en: So you've got a book that is, I suppose, in a way, the fruit of many decades of reflection on the subject of Englishness and England called Who Are We Now?
sentences.zh: 你有一本书，我想在某种程度上，它是你几十年来对英国和英国性思考的结晶，书名叫《我们现在是谁？》

sentences.en: Stories of Modern England.
sentences.zh: 《现代英国的故事》。

sentences.en: Jason, who are we now?
sentences.zh: 杰森，我们现在是谁？

sentences.en: It's a good question, Tom.
sentences.zh: 这是个好问题，汤姆。

sentences.en: And thank you for having me on the show.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我上节目。

sentences.en: It's a great honour to be on this wonderful podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 能参加这个精彩的播客是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: And thank you for reminding me of my captaincy back in the day.
sentences.zh: 也谢谢你提醒我当年的队长经历。

sentences.en: And that was actually a quintessentially Orwellian scene because it was a village called Hatfield Heath, very close to Hatfield Forest in Essex.
sentences.zh: 那其实是一个非常典型的奥威尔式场景，因为那是在埃塞克斯郡哈特菲尔德森林附近的一个叫哈特菲尔德希思的村庄。
zh_words: 埃塞克斯郡哈特菲尔德

sentences.en: And beautiful late September day, if I recall.
sentences.zh: 如果我没记错的话，那是一个美丽的九月下旬的日子。

sentences.en: And it was a sort of gentleman and player's encounter.
sentences.zh: 那是一场绅士与球员的邂逅。

sentences.en: Your brother turned up in an open top classic car.
sentences.zh: 你哥哥开着一辆敞篷经典车出现了。

sentences.en: And a lot of posh Oxbridge types appeared alongside you, of which I am not one.
sentences.zh: 还有很多像你一样时髦的牛剑类型的人，我可不是其中之一。

sentences.en: And then on the opposition were a group of local village cricketers.
sentences.zh: 对手是一群当地的乡村板球运动员。

sentences.en: And the guy who took a liking to your bowling late in the game, actually, Tom, you were bowling your accurate medium pieces.
sentences.zh: 比赛后期，那个喜欢打你投球的家伙，其实汤姆，你当时投的是精准的中速球。

sentences.en: Quick medium, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想是快中速球。

sentences.en: Fast medium.
sentences.zh: 快中速。

sentences.en: Fast medium.
sentences.zh: 快中速。

sentences.en: The local blacksmith sort of took to them with relish.
sentences.zh: 当地的铁匠津津有味地接住了它们。

sentences.en: And they were appearing either over the boundary without bouncing or one bounce.
sentences.zh: 球要么直接飞过边界线，要么落地弹起一次后飞出。

sentences.en: But Jason, I'd lost it in the mind.
sentences.zh: 但杰森，我当时心态崩了。

sentences.en: It's a game played in the mind.
sentences.zh: 这是一种心理博弈。

sentences.en: And you shredded my self-confidence with your man management skills.
sentences.zh: 你用你的管理技巧摧毁了我的自信心。

sentences.en: Indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: I did ask you to be canny, didn't I, if I recall?
sentences.zh: 我记得我确实让你机灵点，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes, you did.
sentences.zh: 是的，你说了。

sentences.en: You did.
sentences.zh: 你确实说了。

sentences.en: Anyway, Dominic began with Orwell.
sentences.zh: 总之，多米尼克是从奥威尔开始的。

sentences.en: Dominic, I think that was from The Lion and the Unicorn, wasn't it?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我想那是出自《狮子与独角兽》，对吧？

sentences.en: It was, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Which Orwell wrote in, began in the spring of 1940 and then completed as the bombs were falling on London during the Blitz in sort of September 1940 and beyond.
sentences.zh: 奥威尔在1940年春天开始写，然后在1940年9月及之后伦敦遭受闪电战轰炸时完成了它。

sentences.en: And he likens England to an awakened giant in that essay.
sentences.zh: 他在那篇文章中把英国比作一个觉醒的巨人。

sentences.en: But always, always worried that England is asleep.
sentences.zh: 但总是，总是担心英国在沉睡。

sentences.en: If you recall, he comes back from Catalonia, where he fought as a volunteer in one of the militias, one of the brigades,
sentences.zh: 如果你还记得，他从加泰罗尼亚回来，在那里他作为志愿者在民兵旅之一战斗，

sentences.en: and was shot in the throat on the Aragon front and almost died.
sentences.zh: 在阿拉贡前线喉部中弹，差点丧命。

sentences.en: And when he comes back from Barcelona, where he feels the Republican government has betrayed the cause, taking their orders from Stalin's Soviet Union, he certainly believed that.
sentences.zh: 当他从巴塞罗那回来时，他觉得共和政府背叛了事业，听命于斯大林的苏联，他对此深信不疑。

sentences.en: He comes back and the book ends with this wonderful vision of England in the south of England.
sentences.zh: 他回来后，书的结尾是对英格兰南部那段美妙的愿景。

sentences.en: And he speaks about England being, sleeping the deep, deep sleep of England.
sentences.zh: 他谈到英国正在沉睡，沉睡在英国那深深的梦境中。

sentences.en: But he's warning them that the English people are about to be awoken by the roar of bombs.
sentences.zh: 但他警告他们，英国人民即将被炸弹的轰鸣声唤醒。

sentences.en: And I think when Orwell's writing in 1940, he's writing about Britain rather than just England, but he uses England.
sentences.zh: 我认为奥威尔在1940年写作时，他谈论的是不列颠而不仅仅是英格兰，但他用了“英格兰”这个词。

sentences.en: So what you spoke about at the beginning of this sense of England being lost within Britishness, or the two being interchangeable.
sentences.zh: 所以你开头提到的那种英格兰在不列颠性中迷失的感觉，或者两者可以互换。

sentences.en: But at that point in September 1940, what was bringing the nation together was a sense of encroaching threat, was danger.
sentences.zh: 但在1940年9月那个时刻，将国家凝聚在一起的是一种迫在眉睫的威胁，是危险。

sentences.en: After Dunkirk, Orwell knew what had to be done.
sentences.zh: 敦刻尔克之后，奥威尔知道必须做什么。

sentences.en: The army had to be brought home and the invasion had to be stopped.
sentences.zh: 军队必须撤回国内，入侵必须被阻止。

sentences.en: And this was a clarifying moment for Orwell.
sentences.zh: 这对奥威尔来说是一个澄清的时刻。

sentences.en: It had always been deeply ambivalent about his relationship with England and Englishness.
sentences.zh: 他一直对自己与英格兰和英国性的关系感到深深的矛盾。

sentences.en: He was an old Etonian, but he hated the public schools.
sentences.zh: 他曾是伊顿公学生，但他讨厌公学制度。

sentences.en: He served as a policeman in Burma and loathed the empire.
sentences.zh: 他在缅甸当过警察，却厌恶帝国。

sentences.en: But at the same time, he loathed the left, what he called book-trained socialism.
sentences.zh: 但同时，他又厌恶左派，即他所说的“书本社会主义”。

sentences.en: So here was this very quarrelsome and sceptical figure.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常爱争辩且多疑的人物。

sentences.en: And suddenly he has this clarifying moment.
sentences.zh: 突然间，他有了这个澄清的时刻。

sentences.en: This is England.
sentences.zh: 这就是英国。

sentences.en: What is England?
sentences.zh: 什么是英国？

sentences.en: And how do we make the nation cohere and come together and find a sense of unity, a moment of heightened peril and danger?
sentences.zh: 在高度危险和危难的时刻，我们如何让国家团结一致，找到一种统一感？

sentences.en: Of a kind, actually, in completely different circumstances that we're seeing in Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 实际上，在完全不同的环境下，这与我们在乌克兰看到的情况类似。

sentences.en: A form of Ukrainian national identity is being formed in war, as it was for the English in 1940 into 1941, which was when Orwell wrote that wonderful essay.
sentences.zh: 一种乌克兰民族认同正在战争中形成，正如1940年到1941年英国人的情况一样，那时奥威尔写下了那篇精彩的文章。

sentences.en: So you obviously think there is an England.
sentences.zh: 所以你显然认为存在一个英格兰。

sentences.en: I do, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，我确实认为。

sentences.en: It's all about it.
sentences.zh: 一切都与此有关。

sentences.en: But Englishness, so let's say 30 or 40 years ago, no one wrote about England or Englishness.
sentences.zh: 但英国性，比如说30或40年前，没人写过关于英格兰或英国性的文章。

sentences.en: I mean, it was a question that simply was never raised, wasn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个从未被提出的问题，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yes, I think there's been a kind of weird awakening of Englishness or a sense of English national identity.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为英国性或英国民族认同感出现了一种奇怪的觉醒。

sentences.en: And it's intensified since 97 and the election of Blair and the devolution reforms and the creation of the Scottish Parliament,
sentences.zh: 自97年布莱尔当选、权力下放改革以及苏格兰议会成立以来，这种感觉愈演愈烈，

sentences.en: when you've also had a simultaneous awakening of Scottish national identity.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，苏格兰民族认同也随之觉醒。

sentences.en: So as the Scots have become more confident or more assertive in their sense of Scottishness, in their sense of national identity, it's naturally forced upon an English,
sentences.zh: 因此，随着苏格兰人在民族认同感上变得更加自信或坚定，这自然迫使英国人，

sentences.en: a reconsideration of who they are and what they want, particularly as the United Kingdom itself is in danger.
sentences.zh: 重新审视他们是谁以及他们想要什么，特别是在联合王国本身处于危险之中时。

sentences.en: I mean, it's fragmented and we had a referendum in 2014, which could have ended, which could have ended the union.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它已经碎片化了，我们在2014年举行了公投，那本可能结束，本可能结束这个联盟。

sentences.en: And Nicola Sturgeon and the SNP are powerful hegemonic, you would say, in Scotland and obviously want a second referendum.
sentences.zh: 尼古拉·斯特金和苏格兰民族党在苏格兰拥有强大的霸权，显然他们想要第二次公投。

sentences.en: So again, it's different from Orwell in 1940, but there is also a sense of threat to Britishness, British identity and the union.
sentences.zh: 所以这再次与1940年的奥威尔不同，但也有一种对不列颠性、不列颠身份和联盟的威胁感。

sentences.en: And it's been a period of enormous change and convulsion in recent years.
sentences.zh: 近年来，这是一个充满巨大变化和动荡的时期。

sentences.en: I mean, if you just have to think about the last sort of seven or eight years with the Scottish independence referendum, the 2015 surprise victory for David Cameron,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你想想过去七八年，苏格兰独立公投，戴维·卡梅伦2015年的意外胜利，

sentences.en: which then led to the 2016 Brexit referendum, the eruption of Corbynism from the left, Trump in America.
sentences.zh: 随后导致了2016年的脱欧公投，左翼科尔宾主义的爆发，美国的特朗普。

sentences.en: And so it goes on.
sentences.zh: 事情还在继续。

sentences.en: And meanwhile, you had this sense of kind of national populism rising through the influence of Nigel Farage and UKIP.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，在奈杰尔·法拉奇和英国独立党的推动下，这种民族民粹主义正在兴起。

sentences.en: So it's been a period of extraordinary change and convulsion and upheaval.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个充满非凡变化、动荡和剧变的时期。

sentences.en: And somewhere amidst this is a rising sense of English identity, often identified, I think, unfairly with reaction and loss and nostalgia.
sentences.zh: 在这之中，英国身份认同感正在上升，我认为这往往被不公平地与反动、失落和怀旧联系在一起。

sentences.en: But I think one could make the case for a progressive and positive sense of modern English identity as well within the greater framework of Britishness.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，在不列颠性的大框架内，我们也可以为现代英国身份认同提出一种进步和积极的论点。

sentences.en: Can I ask a question about the loss and nostalgia?
sentences.zh: 我可以问一个关于失落和怀旧的问题吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 可以。

sentences.en: Because in your introduction, you say one of the things you want to talk about in your book is the stubborn notion that Englishness and loss are inextricable.
sentences.zh: 因为在你的引言中，你说你想在书中讨论的一件事是关于英国性和失落感密不可分的顽固观念。

sentences.en: And there is something unusual about Englishness and nostalgia, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 英国性和怀旧之间确实有些不同寻常之处，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, even when Orwell was writing in 1940, a lot of the things he's talking about, the sort of the rattle of pin tables in the pubs, the old maids,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，即使在1940年奥威尔写作时，他谈论的许多事情，比如酒吧里弹球机的响声，老处女们，

sentences.en: they were old-fashioned even in 1940.
sentences.zh: 即使在1940年，它们也已经过时了。

sentences.en: And there is always this sense with Englishness, particularly now, actually, when people talk about Englishness, they talk about it in terms of it being reactionary backward.
sentences.zh: 英国性总是给人这种感觉，尤其是现在，当人们谈论英国性时，他们谈论的是它作为一种反动和落后的东西。

sentences.en: I mean, you mentioned Nigel Farage.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你提到了奈杰尔·法拉奇。

sentences.en: He's often seen as a kind of – as an avatar of a kind of Englishness.
sentences.zh: 他常被视为某种——某种英格兰精神的化身。

sentences.en: But do you think that's – we've got the wrong idea that there is another – or – well, the job with all these things is so hard to pin down, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 但你认为那是——我们是否对“英格兰精神”存在误解，或者说——好吧，所有这些概念都很难界定，不是吗？

sentences.en: Go on, Tom.
sentences.zh: 继续说，汤姆。

sentences.en: Sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: Well, I was just going to say about that that one of the reasons, perhaps, for that is that England is, as a political entity, incredibly old.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我只是想说，这其中的原因之一，或许是因为英格兰作为一个政治实体，历史极其悠久。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a very – as a – could one say nation-state?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它非常——作为一个——可以称之为民族国家吗？

sentences.en: I mean, as a political construction, it is very, very precocious.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，作为一种政治建构，它非常、非常早熟。

sentences.en: Probably Denmark is its only rival.
sentences.zh: 大概只有丹麦能与它匹敌。

sentences.en: I was about to say, some historians would say England and Denmark are the first two nation-states, wouldn't they?
sentences.zh: 我正想说，有些历史学家会认为英格兰和丹麦是最初的两个民族国家，不是吗？

sentences.en: And so you think people are always looking back to the past and saying things were better in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 所以你认为人们总是回顾过去，说过去的事情更好。

sentences.en: So we've done a lot of stuff on the Civil Wars, and people in the Civil War are looking back to the Anglo-Saxons and saying, well, they were free then, you know,
sentences.zh: 我们研究了很多关于内战的内容，内战时期的人们回顾盎格鲁-撒克逊时代，说，嗯，那时他们是自由的，你知道的，

sentences.en: and then the Normans imposed a yoke.
sentences.zh: 然后诺曼人强加了枷锁。

sentences.en: If only we could get back to the glory days of the Anglo-Saxons.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能回到盎格鲁-撒克逊人的辉煌岁月该多好。

sentences.en: And that basically is a trend that – or John of Gaunt's great speech.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是一种趋势——或者说冈特的约翰那段伟大的演讲。

sentences.en: I mean, you name the passage of Orwell as one of the great meditations on England.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你把奥威尔的那段文字列为关于英格兰最伟大的沉思之一。

sentences.en: But John of Gaunt's speech in Richard II, Shakespeare's play, where he – again, you know, he's – you know,
sentences.zh: 但在莎士比亚的剧作《理查二世》中，冈特的约翰那段演讲，他又一次，你知道，他——你知道，

sentences.en: this wonderful kind of lyrical description of England bound in by the triumphant sea.
sentences.zh: 那种对被胜利之海环绕的英格兰极其美妙的抒情描述。

sentences.en: And yet there, John of Gaunt again is mourning what he sees as English decline.
sentences.zh: 然而，冈特的约翰再次哀悼他所看到的英格兰的衰落。

sentences.en: So it could be that, you know, one of the most traditionally English things is to worry that England is going to the dogs.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，最传统的英格兰式行为之一，可能就是担心英格兰正在走向没落。

sentences.en: That is built in.
sentences.zh: 这是根深蒂固的。

sentences.en: What do you think, Jason?
sentences.zh: 你觉得呢，杰森？

sentences.en: I agree with Tom.
sentences.zh: 我同意汤姆的观点。

sentences.en: Tom,
sentences.zh: 汤姆，

sentences.en: I think I say in the book that there's this sense of something lost or something deeper and purer and more innocent that's been lost flows through the English centuries like an underground stream.
sentences.zh: 我想我在书中说过，那种失去某种东西，或者失去某种更深沉、更纯粹、更天真的东西的感觉，像地下水一样流淌在英格兰的几个世纪里。

sentences.en: And I think it does.
sentences.zh: 我认为确实如此。

sentences.en: And it's there in Shakespeare, Tom, for sure.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这在莎士比亚的作品中肯定存在。

sentences.en: More recently, it was there in Houseman and his wonderful poeMs.
sentences.zh: 最近，它也出现在豪斯曼和他美妙的诗歌中。

sentences.en: It's there in English poetry.
sentences.zh: 它存在于英国诗歌中。

sentences.en: And it goes right back.
sentences.zh: 而且它一直追溯到很久以前。

sentences.en: I mean, I listened some weeks ago to your episode on the Norman conquest and the defeat, the sense of Englishness.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，几周前我听了你关于诺曼征服和失败的那一集，那种英格兰精神的感觉。

sentences.en: It's been founded upon a heroic defeat against the Norman invaders.
sentences.zh: 它是建立在对诺曼入侵者的一次英雄式失败之上的。

sentences.en: But even – and then, you know, what was lost there and what was lost before the conquest going back to an Anglo-Saxon England.
sentences.zh: 但即使是——然后，你知道，那里失去了什么，以及在征服之前失去了什么，追溯到盎格鲁-撒克逊时期的英格兰。

sentences.en: A sense after the conquest that here was an elite that spoke French and the ordinary English man and woman, you know,
sentences.zh: 征服后的一种感觉是，这里有一个说法语的精英阶层，而普通的英格兰男女，你知道，

sentences.en: they didn't – the elites didn't even speak the language that they spoke themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们没有——精英们甚至不说他们自己说的语言。

sentences.en: So I think it's there, a sense of loss, a sense of nostalgia.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为它就在那里，一种失落感，一种怀旧感。

sentences.en: And then, of course, after the Act of Union, 1707, Englishness was lost within Britishness.
sentences.zh: 当然，在1707年《联合法案》之后，英格兰精神在不列颠精神中迷失了。

sentences.en: And the English were encouraged to see themselves, first and foremost, as British in this great imperial project in which the English played their role, as indeed did the Scots.
sentences.zh: 英格兰人被鼓励首先将自己视为大英帝国这一伟大工程中的不列颠人，英格兰人在其中扮演了角色，苏格兰人也确实如此。

sentences.en: So Dominic's right when he said at the beginning that, you know, here's this nation, but it doesn't have its own discrete political institutions.
sentences.zh: 所以多米尼克在开头说得对，你知道，这是一个国家，但它没有自己独立的政治机构。

sentences.en: And therefore, England in recent times hasn't been given the opportunity to reimagine itself, as indeed Scotland has,
sentences.zh: 因此，近年来英格兰没有机会像苏格兰那样重新构想自己，

sentences.en: through the creation of the Scottish Parliament and all of the conversation and debate that has been generated by devolution and what has followed from that.
sentences.zh: 通过建立苏格兰议会，以及权力下放所引发的所有对话和辩论，以及随之而来的一切。

sentences.en: I mean, if you remember George Robertson, the Labour MP, later head of NATO, said that Scottish devolution would kill Scottish nationalism stone dead,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你还记得工党议员、后来的北约秘书长乔治·罗伯逊曾说，苏格兰权力下放将彻底扼杀苏格兰民族主义，

sentences.en: I think was the phrase he used.
sentences.zh: 我想这是他用的措辞。

sentences.en: Well, that didn't turn out as he hoped.
sentences.zh: 好吧，结果并不如他所愿。

sentences.en: But Jason, this idea that the English perhaps have of themselves as a people who are put upon, who have reasons to feel that things have been lost,
sentences.zh: 但杰森，这种英格兰人可能有的自我认知，认为自己是一个受委屈的民族，有理由觉得失去了某些东西，

sentences.en: and Orwell describes them as a gentle people,
sentences.zh: 奥威尔将他们描述为温和的人民，

sentences.en: I imagine that there'll be lots of people listening to this outside England who may feel that this characterisation is perhaps not entirely accurate.
sentences.zh: 我想在英格兰之外听这个节目的人，可能会觉得这种描述或许并不完全准确。

sentences.en: I mean, I would imagine within Great Britain, and certainly within Ireland as well, the idea that the English are, you know, are put upon a nation of flower rangers, cycling, yes,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想在大不列颠内部，当然还有爱尔兰，认为英格兰人是，你知道，是受委屈的，是那种喜欢园艺、骑自行车的人，是的，

sentences.en: exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And of course, you know, England was the most powerful component of the country that established the largest empire in world history.
sentences.zh: 当然，你知道，英格兰是建立世界历史上最大帝国的国家中最强大的部分。

sentences.en: And the English were not gentle in the Caribbean, they were often not gentle in India, Orwell himself, of course, you know, he was a policeman in Burma, absolutely knew that.
sentences.zh: 英格兰人在加勒比地区并不温和，他们在印度也往往不温和，奥威尔本人，当然，你知道，他曾在缅甸当过警察，他完全知道这一点。

sentences.en: There is a sense, isn't there, that Englishness is complicated by the legacy of that, not least because large numbers of people from that empire have now come to England.
sentences.zh: 有一种感觉，不是吗，英格兰精神因为那段遗产而变得复杂，尤其是因为大量来自那个帝国的人现在来到了英格兰。

sentences.en: Yes, and that's, I don't think I said the English were gentle.
sentences.zh: 是的，我不认为我说过英格兰人是温和的。

sentences.en: No, Orwell did.
sentences.zh: 不，是奥威尔说的。

sentences.en: And I think there is this idea still people have that the English are a uniquely kind of gentle people.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们仍然有一种想法，认为英格兰人是一种独特温和的人民。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: When you watch something like the Antiques Roadshow on a Sunday evening on the BBC, I mean, there's a vision of England that many people wish to identify with.
sentences.zh: 当你周日晚上在BBC看《古董巡回秀》之类的节目时，我的意思是，那是许多人希望认同的英格兰愿景。

sentences.en: But of course, go to Newcastle City Centre on a Saturday night, and you see a completely different England.
sentences.zh: 但当然，周六晚上去纽卡斯尔市中心看看，你会看到一个完全不同的英格兰。

sentences.en: Or, you know, I've spent a lot of time on the football terraces over the years, as has Dominic,
sentences.zh: 或者，你知道，多年来我花了很多时间在足球看台上，多米尼克也是，

sentences.en: and certainly the England I witnessed in the late 70s and into the early 80s was brutal and violent.
sentences.zh: 我70年代末到80年代初在看台上看到的英格兰绝对是残酷和暴力的。

sentences.en: And there was an association with, you know, the violence in wider society, what one saw on the terraces.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，看台上所见到的暴力与更广泛社会中的暴力是有联系的。

sentences.en: Orwell also said that he likened the English to a family with the wrong people in charge, in control.
sentences.zh: 奥威尔还说，他把英格兰人比作一个由错误的人掌权、控制的家庭。

sentences.en: So again, he was, you know, he was deeply critical of the empire.
sentences.zh: 所以他再次，你知道，他对帝国进行了深刻的批判。

sentences.en: And that's one of the challenges for anyone writing about Englishness today is this contested identity, and also the past, empire, slavery, colonialism,
sentences.zh: 这就是今天任何撰写关于英格兰精神的人所面临的挑战之一，这是一个充满争议的身份，还有过去、帝国、奴隶制、殖民主义，

sentences.en: the tensions within the British state itself, Ireland, the Irish question, and so on.
sentences.zh: 英国国家内部的紧张局势，爱尔兰，爱尔兰问题等等。

sentences.en: So, I think for those on the left, or many on the left, I mean, they view Englishness with deep suspicion.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为对于左翼人士，或者许多左翼人士来说，我的意思是，他们以深深的怀疑态度看待英格兰精神。

sentences.en: And they're often, as I said at the beginning, associated with reaction, even racism.
sentences.zh: 正如我开头所说，他们经常将其与反动甚至种族主义联系起来。

sentences.en: I mean, the internationalist left are all for celebrating the statehood of others, you know, the Palestinians or the Kurds.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，国际主义左翼热衷于庆祝他人的国家地位，你知道，巴勒斯坦人或库尔德人。

sentences.en: But when it comes to English national identity, they're very, very suspicious.
sentences.zh: 但当涉及到英格兰民族认同时，他们非常、非常怀疑。

sentences.en: And it alarms them.
sentences.zh: 这让他们感到不安。

sentences.en: I think that's fair to say, Dominic, would you?
sentences.zh: 我认为这样说很公平，多米尼克，你觉得呢？

sentences.en: I think, I definitely think it, people are, I mean, well, Orwell commented on that, didn't he, in the, I can't remember whether it was in this essay, in The Lion and the Unicorn,
sentences.zh: 我肯定这么认为，人们是，我的意思是，好吧，奥威尔对此发表过评论，不是吗，在，我不记得是在这篇论文《狮子与独角兽》里，

sentences.en: or whether it was in The Road to Wigan Pier, where he talks about intellectuals who would rather be seen stealing from a poor box in church than standing for God save the king.
sentences.zh: 还是在《通往威根码头之路》里，他谈到那些宁愿被看到从教堂的穷人捐款箱里偷钱，也不愿为“天佑吾王”起立的知识分子。

sentences.en: And I think that that element has always been there.
sentences.zh: 我认为这种成分一直存在。

sentences.en: Not always, surely.
sentences.zh: 不总是这样，肯定不是。

sentences.en: I mean, it's there, isn't it, in the front of the revolutionary period?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它存在，不是吗，在革命时期之前？

sentences.en: I was going to say, in the 18th century, the slightly sort of Tom Payne-ish element.
sentences.zh: 我正想说，在18世纪，那种稍微有点托马斯·潘恩式的成分。

sentences.en: Yeah, but the Whigs, the Whigs.
sentences.zh: 是的，但辉格党人，辉格党人。

sentences.en: So Fox, you know, basically saying the French Revolution is brilliant.
sentences.zh: 所以福克斯，你知道，基本上说法国大革命太棒了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And Napoleon's brilliant.
sentences.zh: 拿破仑太棒了。

sentences.en: And essentially, it's not really about Napoleon's French Revolution.
sentences.zh: 本质上，这并不是真的关于拿破仑的法国大革命。

sentences.en: It's about his dislike of aspects of Tory England.
sentences.zh: 这是关于他不喜欢托利党治下的英格兰的某些方面。

sentences.en: Yeah, but there is a strain within Englishness.
sentences.zh: 是的，但英格兰精神中确实存在一种倾向。

sentences.en: I mean, I don't think other countries have it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我不认为其他国家有这种倾向。

sentences.en: I mean, there is a strain in America that thinks that about people who are very anti-American Americans.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，美国有一种倾向，认为那些非常反美的美国人是这样。

sentences.en: But I think England is probably unusual in having such a profoundly developed sense of anti-patriotism.
sentences.zh: 但我认为英格兰可能很不寻常，因为它有着如此深刻发展的反爱国主义意识。

sentences.en: And why do you think that is?
sentences.zh: 你认为这是为什么？

sentences.en: I don't, I mean, it's a massive question.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，我的意思是，这是一个巨大的问题。

sentences.en: I mean, Tom, you'll be delighted to hear.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，汤姆，你会很高兴听到这个。

sentences.en: I think part of it is religious, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我认为部分原因是宗教性的，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, it's sort of rooted in the, isn't it rooted in the kind of dissenting, Whiggish kind of tradition?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它某种程度上植根于，不是植根于那种异议的、辉格党式的传统吗？

sentences.en: I think it is.
sentences.zh: 我认为是的。

sentences.en: And it's obviously also, don't you think, Jason, a reaction to empire in the 19th century?
sentences.zh: 而且显然，杰森，你不觉得这也是对19世纪帝国的一种反应吗？

sentences.en: And the empire obviously looms enormously large in the mindsets of sort of left-wing English or British intellectuals today, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 帝国显然在今天左翼英格兰或英国知识分子的心态中占据了巨大的位置，不是吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: And when you listen to or even participate in the debates about Englishness and empire, particularly intensification in recent years,
sentences.zh: 当你倾听甚至参与关于英格兰精神和帝国的辩论时，特别是在近年来加剧的辩论，

sentences.en: there's almost a sense of shame at times about the pressure of imperial history weighing on the present.
sentences.zh: 有时几乎有一种羞耻感，因为帝国历史的压力压在现在身上。

sentences.en: But also, I think it's, I go back to the point that it's also a sense of Englishness being lost within Britishness.
sentences.zh: 但我也认为，我回到那个观点，这也是英格兰精神在不列颠精神中迷失的一种感觉。

sentences.en: And there's always a worry about national identity, about ethnicity and blood and soil, certainly.
sentences.zh: 而且人们总是担心民族认同，担心种族、血缘和土地，当然。

sentences.en: And one of the glories of Britishness, I think, is that it was a non-racial, inclusive, plural identity.
sentences.zh: 我认为不列颠精神的荣耀之一在于，它是一种非种族、包容、多元的身份。

sentences.en: We sheltered under this civic umbrella, if that's not a mixed metaphor, of Britishness.
sentences.zh: 我们躲在这个公民伞下，如果这不是一个混合隐喻的话，即不列颠精神。

sentences.en: And I would argue, perhaps better than any other European country, the British have welcomed migrants since the Second World War.
sentences.zh: 我会争辩说，也许比任何其他欧洲国家都好，英国自二战以来一直欢迎移民。

sentences.en: I know there's been terrible racism and hostility, but the modern British state is pretty harmonious, particularly when you compare it with France,
sentences.zh: 我知道存在可怕的种族主义和敌意，但现代英国国家相当和谐，特别是当你把它与法国相比时，

sentences.en: with a distinct neo-fascist right.
sentences.zh: 法国有着明显的各种新法西斯右翼。

sentences.en: We haven't had the emergence of a neo-fascist right in this country.
sentences.zh: 我们这个国家没有出现新法西斯右翼。

sentences.en: But Jason, isn't there a kind of paradox there, perhaps, that since 97, certainly, the rate of immigration into Britain has massively increased?
sentences.zh: 但杰森，这其中难道没有一种悖论吗，或许，自97年以来，进入英国的移民率肯定大幅增加了？

sentences.en: And obviously, not just from Commonwealth countries, but from the European Union.
sentences.zh: 显然，不仅来自英联邦国家，还来自欧盟。

sentences.en: And so the proportion of foreign-born children in England has gone up massively.
sentences.zh: 所以英格兰外国出生的儿童比例大幅上升。

sentences.en: And so you would think that in that period, the salience of Britishness would be all the more important if it is.
sentences.zh: 所以你会认为在那段时期，不列颠精神的显著性会更加重要，如果确实如此的话。

sentences.en: And I agree with you that it's something that kind of transcends the idea of, you know, ancient national roots far more than Englishness or Scottishness or Welshness does.
sentences.zh: 我同意你的观点，它超越了那种，你知道，古老的民族根源，远比英格兰精神、苏格兰精神或威尔士精神更甚。

sentences.en: And yet, it's precisely the more that immigration has gone up, the more the sense of people being English or indeed Scottish has gone up as well.
sentences.zh: 然而，恰恰是移民增加得越多，人们认为自己是英格兰人或苏格兰人的感觉也越强烈。

sentences.en: I mean, do you think it's a kind of degree of cause and effect there?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你认为这其中有一种因果关系吗？

sentences.en: I think there's a chapter about the cockle-picking disaster on Morecambe Bay, 2004.
sentences.zh: 我想书中有一章是关于2004年莫克姆湾的拾蛤惨案。

sentences.en: But within that chapter, I write…
sentences.zh: 但在那一章里，我写道……

sentences.en: So that's when the Chinese labourers were drowned.
sentences.zh: 那是中国劳工溺水的时候。

sentences.en: Yeah, the undocumented Chinese migrants who were working as cockle-pickers.
sentences.zh: 是的，那些作为拾蛤工工作的无证中国移民。

sentences.en: And I tell the story of the lone survivor of that disaster.
sentences.zh: 我讲述了那场灾难中唯一幸存者的故事。

sentences.en: But it happened in 2004.
sentences.zh: 但那是2004年发生的。

sentences.en: And that was also the year when the EU enlarged and opened up to the eastern states.
sentences.zh: 那也是欧盟扩大并向东欧国家开放的那一年。

sentences.en: And I was talking to Nigel Farage about this, because Farage is a figure in the book, inevitably, because he's been such an influential politician, you know,
sentences.zh: 我当时正在和奈杰尔·法拉奇谈论这件事，因为法拉奇是书中的一个人物，不可避免，因为他是一位非常有影响力的政治家，你知道，

sentences.en: one of the most influential post-war politicians.
sentences.zh: 战后最有影响力的政治家之一。

sentences.en: And he said to me that immigration and the EU, they were not an issue until 19… sorry, until 2004.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，移民和欧盟，在19……抱歉，在2004年之前都不是问题。

sentences.en: And then he saw his opportunity to reopen the immigration debate, which he said had been closed down ever since Enoch Powell had delivered his rivers of blood speech.
sentences.zh: 然后他看到了重新开启移民辩论的机会，他说自伊诺克·鲍威尔发表“血河”演讲以来，这个辩论就一直被关闭。

sentences.en: When was it, Dominic, end of the 60s?
sentences.zh: 那是什么时候，多米尼克，60年代末？

sentences.en: 68, that was.
sentences.zh: 68年，就是那时。

sentences.en: So he suddenly saw an opportunity.
sentences.zh: 所以他突然看到了机会。

sentences.en: And he said he was warned by fellow big figures within UKIP not to go there.
sentences.zh: 他说他被英国独立党内其他大人物警告不要碰这个话题。

sentences.en: This would be too dangerous.
sentences.zh: 这太危险了。

sentences.en: But he said it was never about, for him, it was never about ethnicity or race.
sentences.zh: 但他表示，对他来说，这从来不是关于种族或民族的问题。

sentences.en: It was about numbers and a loss of control.
sentences.zh: 这是关于数量和失去控制的问题。

sentences.en: And he was able to manipulate that.
sentences.zh: 他能够操纵这一点。

sentences.en: And don't forget, of the EU member states, it was only the UK, Sweden and Ireland that neglected to impose seven-year transition controls.
sentences.zh: 别忘了，在欧盟成员国中，只有英国、瑞典和爱尔兰忽略了实施七年过渡控制。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So Germany, France, Italy, the other big economies chose to impose the seven-year control.
sentences.zh: 所以德国、法国、意大利，其他大经济体选择实施七年控制。

sentences.en: So they wouldn't accept migrants from the East under free movement rules for seven years.
sentences.zh: 所以他们七年内不会根据自由流动规则接受来自东方的移民。

sentences.en: And the Labour government of the time, the very complacent new Labour governments, said they expected around 8,000 to 13,000 migrants from the Eastern states to arrive per year.
sentences.zh: 而当时的工党政府，那些非常自满的新工党政府，说他们预计每年会有大约8000到13000名来自东欧国家的移民到达。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the true figure was?
sentences.zh: 而真实数字是？

sentences.en: Hundreds and hundreds of thousands.
sentences.zh: 几十万，几十万。

sentences.en: But what it was, Tom, was the largest unplanned migration, surely, in British history.
sentences.zh: 但汤姆，那肯定是英国历史上最大规模的无计划移民。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: But it still doesn't answer the question of why that hasn't amplified people's sense of identity as British rather than, say, English.
sentences.zh: 但这仍然没有回答为什么这没有放大人们作为不列颠人而不是英格兰人的身份认同感。

sentences.en: Because simultaneously, you've had the devolution reforMs.
sentences.zh: 因为与此同时，你进行了权力下放改革。

sentences.en: So when Blair came to power, he gave a speech before he came to power in 1995 where he said, I want this to be a young country.
sentences.zh: 所以当布莱尔上台时，他在1995年上台前发表了一次演讲，他说，我希望这是一个年轻的国家。

sentences.en: And then he said, we will be a young country.
sentences.zh: 然后他说，我们将成为一个年轻的国家。

sentences.en: He never spoke about England.
sentences.zh: 他从未谈论过英格兰。

sentences.en: He was speaking about Britain.
sentences.zh: 他谈论的是英国。

sentences.en: I mean, what an absurd thing to say, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这真是荒谬，汤姆。

sentences.en: You've spoken already about the deep history of England and the notion of an English nation.
sentences.zh: 你已经谈到了英格兰的深厚历史和英格兰民族的概念。

sentences.en: And Blair wanted us to be part of a young country.
sentences.zh: 布莱尔希望我们成为一个年轻国家的一部分。

sentences.en: In other words, he wanted to will a new country into being and push back against the burdens of the past as he would have seen them.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他想凭意志创造一个新国家，并以此回击他眼中那些过去的负担。

sentences.en: And he thought one way of becoming a young country would be through the devolution reforMs.
sentences.zh: 他认为成为年轻国家的一种方式是通过权力下放改革。

sentences.en: But they ignited Scottish nationalism.
sentences.zh: 但这些改革反而点燃了苏格兰民族主义。

sentences.en: Is that, do you think, because, Jason, he didn't understand, my take on that would be that he just, because he didn't feel it himself,
sentences.zh: 杰森，你认为这是因为他不理解吗？我的看法是，他只是因为自己没有那种感受，

sentences.en: he simply didn't understand the cultural and political power of nationalism.
sentences.zh: 所以他根本不理解民族主义在文化和政治上的力量。

sentences.en: So it almost didn't occur to him.
sentences.zh: 这几乎没在他的考虑范围内。

sentences.en: That by creating a Scottish parliament or a Welsh assembly, you would create a focus into which, well,
sentences.zh: 他没意识到，通过建立苏格兰议会或威尔士议会，你会创造一个焦点，或者说，

sentences.en: you'd create a vessel into which people would pour all these energies which had lain dormant for so long.
sentences.zh: 你会创造一个容器，让人们将那些沉睡已久的能量倾注其中。

sentences.en: Do you think that's, he just didn't get that?
sentences.zh: 你觉得是这样吗？他只是没意识到这一点？

sentences.en: I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 我想你是对的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And also, what he didn't understand was there was a restiveness out there in what you might call deep England, in the shires, the smaller county towns and neglected coastal towns.
sentences.zh: 而且，他没理解的是，在所谓的“深层英格兰”——那些郡县、较小的城镇和被忽视的沿海城镇中，存在着一种不安情绪。

sentences.en: You know, the town I grew up in, the town I grew up in, Harlow, Newtown, for example, where people felt shut out, they felt neglected, they felt ignored,
sentences.zh: 你知道，比如我长大的那个城镇，哈洛新城，人们感到被排斥、被忽视、被冷落，

sentences.en: they felt mocked and ridiculed by a certain kind of elite.
sentences.zh: 他们感到被某种精英阶层嘲笑和戏弄。

sentences.en: And they were anxious about the forces unleashed by free market globalization, inevitably.
sentences.zh: 而且他们不可避免地对自由市场全球化所释放的力量感到焦虑。

sentences.en: And, you know, globalization lifted hundreds of millions of people out of poverty, notably in China.
sentences.zh: 当然，全球化让数亿人摆脱了贫困，特别是在中国。

sentences.en: And the transnational elites, they benefited enormously from globalization and indeed from free movement.
sentences.zh: 跨国精英们从全球化，甚至从自由流动中获益匪浅。

sentences.en: But there were many losers and many of those losers were in the small towns of England.
sentences.zh: 但也有许多输家，其中许多就生活在英格兰的小城镇里。

sentences.en: But just to stick up for Tony.
sentences.zh: 不过，还是得为托尼说几句公道话。

sentences.en: Yeah, you go ahead, Tom.
sentences.zh: 好，你说吧，汤姆。

sentences.en: Okay, so the idea of England being a young country, and let's focus on England rather than Britain.
sentences.zh: 好的，关于英格兰是一个年轻国家的想法，我们专注于英格兰而不是英国。

sentences.en: Yes, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的。

sentences.en: We've talked about its antiquity.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论过它的古老。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The sense that perhaps that foreigners have of England is indeed of ancient monuments and tradition and beef eaters and all that kind of paraphernalia.
sentences.zh: 外国人对英格兰的印象确实是古迹、传统、御林卫士以及诸如此类的东西。

sentences.en: But since the Second World War, England has quite successfully reinvented itself as a young country, to the degree that it is probably, you know, head for head,
sentences.zh: 但自二战以来，英格兰已经相当成功地将自己重塑为一个年轻国家，以至于它可能，你知道，人均而言，

sentences.en: the most influential proponent of youth culture in the world.
sentences.zh: 是世界上最具影响力的青年文化倡导者。

sentences.en: Swinging London, punk, raves, all that kind of malarkey.
sentences.zh: 摇摆伦敦、朋克、锐舞，诸如此类的玩意儿。

sentences.en: You sound like a high court judge, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你听起来像个高等法院法官。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: But it's all been part of the English brand.
sentences.zh: 但这都是英格兰品牌的一部分。

sentences.en: And you could say that, in a sense, London, for instance, which is the English capital as well as the British capital,
sentences.zh: 你可以说，在某种意义上，伦敦——既是英格兰首都也是英国首都，

sentences.en: is definitely a young city or it has seen itself as being a young city.
sentences.zh: 绝对是一座年轻的城市，或者说它将自己视为一座年轻城市。

sentences.en: But London doesn't feel like an English – I mean, I don't want to sound pharagist, but I don't want to sound pharagiSt.
sentences.zh: 但伦敦感觉不像英格兰——我是说，我不想听起来像法拉奇，但我不想听起来像法拉奇。

sentences.en: London feels British, but I don't think you would go to London and say this feels like the England of deep England.
sentences.zh: 伦敦感觉很“英国”，但我觉得你不会去到伦敦然后说，这感觉就像深层英格兰。

sentences.en: No, of course it doesn't.
sentences.zh: 不，当然不是。

sentences.en: Of course, by definition, because Longleterre Profonde, you know, is not London.
sentences.zh: 当然，从定义上讲，因为“深层英格兰”并不是伦敦。

sentences.en: I mean, that's the whole point.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这正是关键所在。

sentences.en: That's the whole point of it.
sentences.zh: 这正是问题的核心。

sentences.en: But it is, I think, you know, it focuses, again, this question that I'm kind of just chipping away at, which is it does feel like it's the British capital.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，这再次聚焦于我一直在探讨的问题，那就是它确实感觉像是英国的首都。

sentences.en: It's a British city.
sentences.zh: 这是一座英国城市。

sentences.en: It's a city full of Black British, Asian British, Irish British, you know, all these kind of different permutations of British you have.
sentences.zh: 这是一座充满英籍黑人、英籍亚裔、英籍爱尔兰人，你知道，各种不同组合的英国人的城市。

sentences.en: But it's more difficult to attach those labels to English, Black English, Asian English, Irish English.
sentences.zh: 但要给这些标签加上“英格兰”的前缀就难多了，比如英格兰黑人、英格兰亚裔、英格兰爱尔兰人。

sentences.en: I mean, there's a kind of hint of paradox almost there.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这几乎带有一种悖论的意味。

sentences.en: So why is it that with the amplification of immigration, with absolutely the sense that London is now not just, you know, it's not just the British, it's not just European,
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么随着移民的增加，随着伦敦现在不仅是英国的，也不仅仅是欧洲的，

sentences.en: it's absolutely a global city.
sentences.zh: 它绝对是一座全球性城市，

sentences.en: Why has that Britishness, the quality of Britishness, slightly been occluded by the growth of Englishness?
sentences.zh: 为什么那种“英国性”的特质，反而被“英格兰性”的增长稍微掩盖了呢？

sentences.en: I mean, it does seem a slight paradox there.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这看起来确实有点矛盾。

sentences.en: It does, but it's because so many people, I think, feel shut out from that Britishness, that sense of modern Britishness that you've rightly celebrated, Tom, you know,
sentences.zh: 确实如此，但我认为这是因为很多人感到被那种“英国性”排斥在外了，那种你刚才正确赞扬的现代英国性，汤姆，你知道，

sentences.en: the modern London that you and I know and love.
sentences.zh: 你我所熟知并热爱的现代伦敦。

sentences.en: There's a lot, there's a sense that that isn't the country that many,
sentences.zh: 很多人觉得那并不是他们心中的国家，

sentences.en: I'm thinking in particular of many of those people who were attracted by the rhetoric of Farage in particular and UKIP.
sentences.zh: 我特别想到那些被法拉奇和英国独立党的言论所吸引的人。

sentences.en: They don't feel attracted by that modern, cosmopolitan London, Britishness, and nor do the Scots, actually.
sentences.zh: 他们对那种现代、国际化的伦敦式英国性并不感兴趣，其实苏格兰人也不感兴趣。

sentences.en: I remember, I can't speak the whole of the Scots, but I remember Alex Salmon, I invited him to come down to London to give a lecture during the 2014 independence campaign.
sentences.zh: 我记得，我不能代表所有苏格兰人，但我记得亚历克斯·萨蒙德，我在2014年独立运动期间邀请他来伦敦演讲。

sentences.en: And he likened London to a dark star, sucking the energy forces from the rest of the United KingdoMs.
sentences.zh: 他把伦敦比作一颗黑星，吸干了联合王国其余部分的能量。

sentences.en: It draws more and more people to London.
sentences.zh: 它吸引了越来越多的人来到伦敦。

sentences.en: But I said, Alex, hold on here.
sentences.zh: 但我说，亚历克斯，等等。

sentences.en: London also has some of the most impoverished boroughs in the country.
sentences.zh: 伦敦也有这个国家最贫困的一些行政区。

sentences.en: There's deep intergenerational inequality and poverty in London.
sentences.zh: 伦敦存在着深层的代际不平等和贫困。

sentences.en: You know, it's a wonderful, diverse city.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一座美妙、多元的城市。

sentences.en: It's a city of really interconnecting villages.
sentences.zh: 这是一座由真正相互连接的村庄组成的城市。

sentences.en: I mean, there is a deep history of London, Tom, that you understand and well know.
sentences.zh: 我是说，伦敦有着深厚的历史，汤姆，你对此非常了解。

sentences.en: As you walk the streets of London, one is haunted by the ghost traces of what has been before.
sentences.zh: 当你走在伦敦的街道上，你会为过去留下的幽灵痕迹所困扰。

sentences.en: You know, my father came out of the East End and always used to speak very fondly about the old Jewish East End that exists almost today as a kind of ghost traces, as it were.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我父亲来自东区，他总是深情地谈论那个古老的犹太东区，它今天几乎只作为一种幽灵痕迹存在。

sentences.en: W.G.
sentences.zh: W.G.

sentences.en: Zebold wrote about so beautifully, I think, in Austerlitz.
sentences.zh: 塞巴尔德在《奥斯特利茨》中写得非常美。

sentences.en: So there is a paradox and these are the paradoxes that I'm trying to work away at in the book as I try and understand who we are today.
sentences.zh: 所以这里存在一个悖论，而这些正是我在书中试图解决的悖论，因为我试图理解我们今天是谁。

sentences.en: You know, what is England and what these huge, huge forces have done to the country in recent times.
sentences.zh: 你知道，什么是英格兰，以及这些巨大的力量在最近一段时间对这个国家做了什么。

sentences.en: There's a wonderful line from The Lion and the Unicorn, such a great essay, if you want to think about these questions,
sentences.zh: 《狮子与独角兽》里有一句精彩的话，如果你想思考这些问题，那真是一篇伟大的文章，

sentences.en: where Orwell says it is of the deepest importance to try and determine what England is before guessing what part England can play in the huge events that are happening.
sentences.zh: 奥威尔在文中说，在猜测英格兰能在正在发生的巨大事件中扮演什么角色之前，确定英格兰究竟是什么，具有极其重要的意义。

sentences.en: And that's really the question that's informed the book and that I've attempted to answer, not with any certainty, but I play with some of these paradoxes, Tom,
sentences.zh: 这确实是贯穿全书的问题，也是我试图回答的问题，虽然没有确切答案，但我探讨了其中的一些悖论，汤姆，

sentences.en: that you're rightly raising.
sentences.zh: 正如你所指出的那样。

sentences.en: Let's take a break now.
sentences.zh: 我们现在休息一下。

sentences.en: And when we come back, we will play with more paradoxes and continue and continue our search for England.
sentences.zh: 回来后，我们将探讨更多的悖论，并继续我们对英格兰的探索。

sentences.en: And that will be England gone.
sentences.zh: 而那将是逝去的英格兰。

sentences.en: The shadows, the meadows, the lanes, the guild halls, the carved choirs.
sentences.zh: 阴影、草地、小巷、行会大厅、雕刻的唱诗班席位。

sentences.en: There'll be books.
sentences.zh: 书本还会存在。

sentences.en: It will linger on in galleries.
sentences.zh: 它会在画廊里徘徊。

sentences.en: But all that remains for us will be concrete and tyres.
sentences.zh: 但留给我们的将只有混凝土和轮胎。

sentences.en: That was the ever cheerful Philip Larkin, writing, I think, back in the 60s.
sentences.zh: 那是永远乐观的菲利普·拉金，我想他是在60年代写的。

sentences.en: And Jason, one of the things that strikes me about England is that the English are famously animal lovers.
sentences.zh: 杰森，关于英格兰，有一点让我印象深刻，那就是英格兰人以爱动物闻名。

sentences.en: They love their countryside and more people belong to wildlife support groups than in any other country in the world.
sentences.zh: 他们热爱乡村，加入野生动物支持组织的人数比世界上任何其他国家都多。

sentences.en: And yet we have some of the most, you know, we are one of the most environmentally depleted countries anywhere.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们却是环境破坏最严重的国家之一。

sentences.en: Where our biodiversity is in a constant case state of crisis.
sentences.zh: 我们的生物多样性正处于持续的危机状态。

sentences.en: I wonder, England is actually quite a small country.
sentences.zh: 我想知道，英格兰其实是一个很小的国家。

sentences.en: Is there a sense that the rising population in England is generating these anxieties about wither England simply because there isn't actually that much of it?
sentences.zh: 是否有一种感觉，即英格兰不断增长的人口正在引发对英格兰未来的焦虑，仅仅是因为它实际上并没有那么大？

sentences.en: And that the more people there are, the more it will turn into concrete and tyres and the more kind of hedgehogs and hedgerows will vanish.
sentences.zh: 而且人越多，它就越会变成混凝土和轮胎，刺猬和树篱也会消失得越多。

sentences.en: What is the population of England?
sentences.zh: 英格兰的人口是多少？

sentences.en: Is it about 58 million, 57 million?
sentences.zh: 是5800万还是5700万左右？

sentences.en: The population of the UK is almost 70 million and England is by far, I mean, it's about 60 million, I would have said.
sentences.zh: 英国的人口接近7000万，而英格兰占了绝大多数，我想说大约有6000万。

sentences.en: And it is a relatively small landmass and a small country.
sentences.zh: 它是一个相对较小的陆地面积和较小的国家。

sentences.en: And I think that's also one of the anxieties that drives the debate about the British Union.
sentences.zh: 我认为这也是驱动关于英国联盟辩论的焦虑之一。

sentences.en: If Scotland was to become an independent country, then England or British Britain would lose or England would lose access to so much of the territorial waters and the landmass.
sentences.zh: 如果苏格兰成为一个独立国家，那么英格兰或英国将失去对大部分领海和陆地的控制。

sentences.en: I think Scotland is about a third of the island of Great Britain in size.
sentences.zh: 我认为苏格兰的面积大约是大不列颠岛的三分之一。

sentences.en: But yes, Tom, I think a lot of people, I think, associate England and Englishness with landscape, particularly the countryside.
sentences.zh: 但是的，汤姆，我认为很多人将英格兰和英格兰性与景观联系在一起，特别是乡村。

sentences.en: Yeah, green and pleasant land.
sentences.zh: 是的，绿色宜人的土地。

sentences.en: Green and pleasant land.
sentences.zh: 绿色宜人的土地。

sentences.en: You've got Larkin there.
sentences.zh: 你提到了拉金。

sentences.en: I mentioned Houseman's beautiful poems earlier, the Elegies, Wordsworth, the romantic tradition about which, Tom, you've written so well, particularly about Byron.
sentences.zh: 我之前提到了豪斯曼美丽的诗歌，挽歌，华兹华斯，浪漫主义传统，关于这些，汤姆，你写得很好，特别是关于拜伦。

sentences.en: Although he liked to wander the Alps, didn't he, rather than the Cotswolds.
sentences.zh: 尽管他喜欢漫游阿尔卑斯山，而不是科茨沃尔德。

sentences.en: He cleared out of England very quickly.
sentences.zh: 他很快就离开了英格兰。

sentences.en: I was about to say, you say about Tom writing about Byron, but doesn't your Byron turn out to be a vampire, Tom?
sentences.zh: 我正想说，你说汤姆写了拜伦，但你的拜伦最后不是变成了吸血鬼吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: Yeah, he does.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实。

sentences.en: Yeah, he does.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实。

sentences.en: He's a rootless cosmopolitan, the very worst kind.
sentences.zh: 他是一个无根的国际主义者，最糟糕的那种。

sentences.en: But there is a constant pressure on the English landscape.
sentences.zh: 但英格兰的景观一直承受着压力。

sentences.en: One sees these debates around some of the small rural towns which are being built around.
sentences.zh: 人们可以看到围绕一些正在进行建设的农村小镇的辩论。

sentences.en: And I think the phrase is donutted by new modern estates.
sentences.zh: 我想那个词是“被现代新庄园包围”。

sentences.en: And at the same time, young people say, we know we need somewhere to live.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，年轻人说，我们知道我们需要住的地方。

sentences.en: We need more housing.
sentences.zh: 我们需要更多的住房。

sentences.en: And it's, again, it's one of the tensions that defines the country today.
sentences.zh: 这再次成为定义当今国家的紧张关系之一。

sentences.en: You know, I don't, I'm not anxious about a rising population.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我不担心人口增长。

sentences.en: In many ways, I kind of welcome that sort of boisterous, clamorous exchange of ideas and individuals.
sentences.zh: 在很多方面，我反而欢迎那种充满活力、喧闹的思想和个人的交流。

sentences.en: You live in Brixton, Tom, so you obviously relish city life.
sentences.zh: 你住在布里克斯顿，汤姆，所以你显然很享受城市生活。

sentences.en: Dominic is a rural man out in the Cotswolds.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克是个住在科茨沃尔德的农村人。

sentences.en: Exactly, yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错，是的。

sentences.en: I live in a very bland, suburban town.
sentences.zh: 我住在一个非常平淡的郊区城镇。

sentences.en: So I do live in Brixton, which is kind of almost the archetype of the inner city.
sentences.zh: 我确实住在布里克斯顿，这几乎是内城的原型。

sentences.en: But I grew up outside Salisbury.
sentences.zh: 但我是在索尔兹伯里外长大的。

sentences.en: You did.
sentences.zh: 你确实是。

sentences.en: And I want to feel that those green fields are still there.
sentences.zh: 我希望感觉到那些绿色的田野依然存在。

sentences.en: But that's where so much of this countryside stuff comes from.
sentences.zh: 但这就是很多乡村情结的来源。

sentences.en: So I was thinking when Jason was talking, one of the, I mean, he used to be famous.
sentences.zh: 当杰森说话时，我在想，其中一个，我是说，他曾经很有名。

sentences.en: He's not famous anymore.
sentences.zh: 他现在不出名了。

sentences.en: But one of the politically very famous iterations of that was Stanley Baldwin in the 1920s.
sentences.zh: 但在政治上非常著名的迭代之一是1920年代的斯坦利·鲍德温。

sentences.en: Very much a friend of the show.
sentences.zh: 他是节目的老朋友了。

sentences.en: England is the country and the country is England.
sentences.zh: 英格兰就是乡村，乡村就是英格兰。

sentences.en: Or the other way around, I can't remember which.
sentences.zh: 或者反过来，我不记得是哪一个了。

sentences.en: But he did that at precisely the moment when England was becoming very suburban.
sentences.zh: 但他是在英格兰变得非常郊区化的那一刻说出这句话的。

sentences.en: You know, his was a message crafted for people.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他的信息是为人们精心打造的。

sentences.en: Ribbon developments along the way.
sentences.zh: 沿途的带状开发。

sentences.en: Yeah, listening on radios in new suburban developments who wanted to believe.
sentences.zh: 是的，在新的郊区开发项目中听着收音机，想要相信的人们。

sentences.en: That there was, you know, their house is called the Larches or something.
sentences.zh: 他们的房子叫“落叶松”之类的名字。

sentences.en: But as you say, they live, they can't see any Larches.
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，他们住在那儿，却看不到任何落叶松。

sentences.en: And I think that, doesn't that explain?
sentences.zh: 我想，这难道不能解释吗？

sentences.en: England is one of the most densely populated countries in Europe.
sentences.zh: 英格兰是欧洲人口最稠密的国家之一。

sentences.en: I think only in the Netherlands and Belgium.
sentences.zh: 我想仅次于荷兰和比利时。

sentences.en: But absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And you also saw a reworking of Baldwin and indeed George Orwell in some of John Major's speeches late in his premiership.
sentences.zh: 你还在约翰·梅杰首相任期末的一些演讲中看到了鲍德温甚至乔治·奥威尔思想的重现。

sentences.en: Although indeed another Brixton boy.
sentences.zh: 尽管他也是个布里克斯顿男孩。

sentences.en: Well, he quoted, didn't he?
sentences.zh: 嗯，他引用了，不是吗？

sentences.en: The old maids riding into communion through mists, all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 老处女们骑马穿过薄雾去领圣餐，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: He did.
sentences.zh: 他确实引用了。

sentences.en: And shadows stretching across county grounds.
sentences.zh: 还有阴影掠过郡板球场。

sentences.en: And there was a sense of this kind of rural idyll.
sentences.zh: 有一种乡村田园诗的感觉。

sentences.en: Again, but that plays back to our original idea of something that's loSt.
sentences.zh: 同样，这又回到了我们最初关于某种“失去的东西”的想法。

sentences.en: Something we had.
sentences.zh: 我们曾经拥有的东西。

sentences.en: And something we've let go.
sentences.zh: 以及我们已经放手的东西。

sentences.en: Or has been taken away.
sentences.zh: 或者已经被夺走的东西。

sentences.en: It's an anxiety that that specifically goes back to the Industrial Revolution, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我想，这是一种可以追溯到工业革命时期的焦虑。

sentences.en: The more England becomes urbanized, the more salient the natural world, the beautiful fields, the wildlife, all that kind of stuff becomes.
sentences.zh: 英格兰城市化程度越高，自然世界、美丽的田野、野生动物以及诸如此类的事物就越显得突出。

sentences.en: I mean, people may not necessarily go and see it, but they want to know that it's there.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，人们未必会亲自去观赏，但他们希望知道这些东西就在那里。

sentences.en: One other thing, Jason, that you mentioned in the first half that I wanted to come back to, because you talk about this quite a lot in the book.
sentences.zh: 杰森，还有一件事，你在上半场提过，我想再回来谈谈，因为你在书中对此谈论了很多。

sentences.en: And I know you've written brilliantly about it in the past, is football.
sentences.zh: 而且我知道你过去曾对此有过精彩的论述，那就是足球。

sentences.en: So football is one of the most famous English exports.
sentences.zh: 足球是英格兰最著名的出口产品之一。

sentences.en: And football is central to England.
sentences.zh: 足球对英格兰至关重要。

sentences.en: I mean, actually, football, a lot of our listeners are not British.
sentences.zh: 其实，关于足球，我们有很多听众并不是英国人。

sentences.en: And they may find this frivolous or mystifying.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会觉得这很轻浮，或者令人困惑。

sentences.en: I would argue that football is probably the single most important vehicle of Englishness.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，足球大概是英格兰精神最重要的载体。

sentences.en: And you talk in your book about the England football team and, for example, the black players.
sentences.zh: 你在书中谈到了英格兰足球队，比如其中的黑人球员。

sentences.en: So there, surely, there is an example of how you can be.
sentences.zh: 所以，这无疑是一个关于你如何能够成为（英格兰人）的例子。

sentences.en: I mean, Tom said black English.
sentences.zh: 我是说，汤姆提到了“黑人英格兰人”。

sentences.en: It's true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: It doesn't trip off the tongue as readily as black British does.
sentences.zh: 它不像“黑人英国人”那样朗朗上口。

sentences.en: But there are clearly, I mean, some of the great icons of Englishness, Raheem Sterling is a good example, are black, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 但显然，英格兰精神的一些伟大象征——拉希姆·斯特林就是一个很好的例子——他们是黑人，不是吗？

sentences.en: Indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: And I think the England football team is a mirror in which we can see the changing face of the nation.
sentences.zh: 我认为英格兰足球队是一面镜子，从中我们可以看到这个国家不断变化的面貌。

sentences.en: I think football is a real, it's a signifier of so much, but particularly of national identity.
sentences.zh: 我认为足球是一个真正的标志，它象征着很多东西，尤其是民族认同感。

sentences.en: I remember going to the England-Scotland match at Euro 96 at Wembley, the famous match where Gascoigne flipped the ball over, was it Colin Hendry?
sentences.zh: 我记得去温布利看了96年欧洲杯英格兰对苏格兰的那场比赛，就是那场著名的比赛，加斯科因把球挑过——是科林·亨德利吗？

sentences.en: It was Colin Hendry, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是科林·亨德利，没错。

sentences.en: And slotted home.
sentences.zh: 然后射门得分。

sentences.en: Glorious goal.
sentences.zh: 精彩的进球。

sentences.en: Beautiful, warm, sunny day in London.
sentences.zh: 伦敦一个美丽、温暖、阳光明媚的日子。

sentences.en: And when I arrived at the stadium, I remember being absolutely shocked to see so many, the flag of St. George everywhere.
sentences.zh: 当我到达体育场时，我记得看到到处都是圣乔治旗，我感到非常震惊。

sentences.en: Whereas if you look back at footage, say, of the 1966 World Cup at Wembley, which was England against West Germany, Bobby Moore's great team that won the World Cup.
sentences.zh: 而如果你回顾一下比如1966年温布利世界杯的录像，那是英格兰对阵西德，博比·摩尔那支赢得世界杯的伟大球队。

sentences.en: But the crowd, everyone's got the Union flag.
sentences.zh: 但观众席上，每个人拿的都是英国国旗（米字旗）。

sentences.en: Even the World Cup mascot, the tournament was held in England, wears a little Union Jack veSt.
sentences.zh: 甚至连世界杯吉祥物，因为锦标赛是在英格兰举办的，都穿着一件印有小米字旗的背心。

sentences.en: I think it's a little lion wears a Union Jack waistcoat or veSt.
sentences.zh: 我想那是一只穿着米字旗马甲或背心的小狮子。

sentences.en: So the iconography of Englishness was actually British iconography.
sentences.zh: 所以，英格兰精神的肖像实际上是英国的肖像。

sentences.en: But suddenly something happened around the time of Euro 96, a year before Blair is elected.
sentences.zh: 但突然间，在96年欧洲杯前后，也就是布莱尔当选前一年，发生了一些变化。

sentences.en: And it's not a top-down, state-directed process.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个自上而下、由国家主导的过程。

sentences.en: It's something that comes from below.
sentences.zh: 它是自下而上产生的。

sentences.en: And one of the means through which it is expressed is football and the English national football team.
sentences.zh: 而表达这一点的途径之一就是足球和英格兰国家足球队。

sentences.en: And for a long time, particularly the late 1970s into the early 80s, English football, the English national football team, was associated with hooliganism.
sentences.zh: 很长一段时间，特别是从70年代末到80年代初，英格兰足球、英格兰国家足球队与足球流氓联系在一起。

sentences.en: But particularly sort of far-right factions, racist factions.
sentences.zh: 特别是某种极右翼派系、种族主义派系。

sentences.en: And there was some terrible violence when England went overseas.
sentences.zh: 当英格兰队去海外比赛时，发生了一些可怕的暴力事件。

sentences.en: I remember there was a great goal that John Barnes scored in Brazil, England-Brazil, in the early 80s, I think.
sentences.zh: 我记得80年代初在巴西，英格兰对阵巴西，约翰·巴恩斯打进了一个精彩的进球，我想是这样。

sentences.en: John Barnes, the black winger who played for Watford and then Liverpool, he scored a wonderful solo goal.
sentences.zh: 约翰·巴恩斯，那位曾效力于沃特福德和利物浦的黑人边锋，他打进了一个精彩的单刀球。

sentences.en: And some of the thugs who had followed England to Brazil said England had won the match 1-0 rather than 2-0 because one of those goals had been scored by a black man.
sentences.zh: 而一些跟随英格兰队去巴西的暴徒却说，英格兰队是以1-0而不是2-0赢得了比赛，因为其中一个进球是由一个黑人打进的。

sentences.en: I mean, a monstrous comment to have made.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这真是一个极其恶劣的评论。

sentences.en: But fast forward to the present day, particularly what we witnessed last summer, Euro 2020, but delayed by a year because of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 但快进到今天，特别是我们去年夏天目睹的一切，2020年欧洲杯，虽然因为疫情推迟了一年。

sentences.en: And we saw this kind of wonderful flourishing of English national identity, as expressed through the English football team,
sentences.zh: 我们看到了这种英格兰民族认同感的奇妙繁荣，正如通过英格兰足球队所表达的那样，

sentences.en: with many of our leading players being black English players.
sentences.zh: 我们许多领军球员都是黑人英格兰球员。

sentences.en: And they were very comfortable embracing the flag of St. George, wrapping themselves in the flag of St. George.
sentences.zh: 他们非常乐于拥抱圣乔治旗，把自己包裹在圣乔治旗中。

sentences.en: Rashford himself identified very strongly with a sense of benevolent Englishness.
sentences.zh: 拉什福德本人就强烈认同一种仁慈的英格兰精神。

sentences.en: And I think England are very fortunate that through these years of polarisation and upheaval and turmoil, they've had Gareth Southgate as their coach,
sentences.zh: 我认为英格兰非常幸运，在这些年的两极分化、动荡和混乱中，他们拥有加雷斯·索斯盖特作为教练，

sentences.en: who is an extraordinarily thoughtful man and has thought very deeply about English national identity.
sentences.zh: 他是一个非常有思想的人，对英格兰民族认同感思考得非常深刻。

sentences.en: I think at the time of the 2018 World Cup in Russia, Southgate said that we, the English, had been a little bit lost in our identity.
sentences.zh: 我想在2018年俄罗斯世界杯期间，索斯盖特曾说，我们英格兰人在身份认同上有点迷失了。

sentences.en: And I hope through my young team, because of their youth and their diversity, we can offer another vision of Englishness.
sentences.zh: 我希望通过我年轻的团队，因为他们的年轻和多元化，我们能提供另一种英格兰精神的愿景。

sentences.en: I mean, Theresa May wouldn't say that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，特蕾莎·梅是不会那样说的。

sentences.en: Jeremy Corbyn wouldn't say that at the time.
sentences.zh: 杰里米·科尔宾当时也不会那样说。

sentences.en: But Southgate leaned into the debates around Englishness and identity.
sentences.zh: 但索斯盖特倾身投入了关于英格兰精神和身份认同的辩论中。

sentences.en: And then just before the Euros last summer, he wrote an essay, which was published on the Players' Tribune, called Dear England, which was an attempt to address, Tom,
sentences.zh: 去年夏天欧洲杯前夕，他写了一篇文章，发表在《球员论坛报》上，题为《亲爱的英格兰》，这是为了回应，汤姆，

sentences.en: the controversies around the Black Lives Matter debate and his team taking the knee.
sentences.zh: 围绕“黑人的命也是命”辩论以及他球队下跪行为的争议。

sentences.en: And he located himself in a tradition.
sentences.zh: 他将自己置于一种传统之中。

sentences.en: His grandfather had served in the Second World War.
sentences.zh: 他的祖父曾在第二次世界大战中服役。

sentences.en: He spoke about his love of the Queen, of the monarchy, of the military, but at the same time spoke about his embrace of more progressive causes.
sentences.zh: 他谈到了他对女王、君主制、军队的热爱，但同时也谈到了他对更进步事业的拥抱。

sentences.en: And it was a fantastic essay, I thought, and wonderfully argued.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一篇精彩的文章，论证得非常出色。

sentences.en: And what he was basically saying was diversity and tradition can go together.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是在说，多元化和传统是可以共存的。

sentences.en: They don't have to be mutually exclusive.
sentences.zh: 它们不必是相互排斥的。

sentences.en: One can inform the other in positive and constructive ways.
sentences.zh: 两者可以以积极和建设性的方式相互促进。

sentences.en: And I think Southgate's England have done more than most to unite many behind the sense of progressive Englishness, I think.
sentences.zh: 我认为索斯盖特的英格兰队在团结人们支持进步的英格兰精神方面做得比大多数人都要多。

sentences.en: But Jason, a slightly more jaundiced take on the mirror that football holds up to England would surely be that for most fans,
sentences.zh: 但是杰森，如果对足球这面映照英格兰的镜子持一种稍微冷嘲热讽的态度，那么对于大多数球迷来说，

sentences.en: and I'm aware that both of you are much keener fans than I am, but I would guess that clubs are much more important ultimately than perhaps the national team.
sentences.zh: 我知道你们俩比我更狂热，但我猜对于球迷来说，俱乐部最终可能比国家队更重要。

sentences.en: And those clubs, there's the idea that jumpers for goalposts, local boys growing up, going through the various squads and then playing for their local team.
sentences.zh: 而那些俱乐部，有一种理念是“以跳线为门柱”，当地男孩成长起来，经历各种梯队，然后为当地球队效力。

sentences.en: I mean, that's the kind of the fantasy that club teams embody.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是俱乐部球队所体现的那种幻想。

sentences.en: And it is a complete fantasy, as you well know.
sentences.zh: 正如你所知，这完全是一种幻想。

sentences.en: Because basically, the club, particularly the absolute elite clubs, are basically, as we've been seeing very recently,
sentences.zh: 因为基本上，俱乐部，特别是那些顶尖俱乐部，基本上，正如我们最近所看到的，

sentences.en: ways for various kleptocrats and oligarchs to wash their dirty linen.
sentences.zh: 是各种盗贼统治者和寡头洗白他们肮脏勾当的途径。

sentences.en: In a way, football is the embodiment of everything that the little man out in the provincial town feels about globalization.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，足球体现了小城镇里的普通人对全球化的所有感受。

sentences.en: That everything that, you know, everything that was local is now a kind of a tiny cog in the great churning machine that is globalization.
sentences.zh: 你知道，曾经属于地方的一切，现在都成了全球化这台巨大轰鸣机器中的一个小齿轮。

sentences.en: Well, just to jump in before Jason, I mean, isn't that what that Super League furore, which was an extraordinary moment.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在杰森开口之前我想插一句，我的意思是，那场“超级联赛”的风波不正是如此吗？那是一个非凡的时刻。

sentences.en: I mean, such a huge story for a few days.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，几天之内就成了如此巨大的新闻。

sentences.en: Isn't that what it encapsulated, Tom?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，那不正是它所概括的吗？

sentences.en: The idea that something profoundly English had been hollowed out and was about to be lost and the local was about to be utterly crushed by the kind of, by this idea of an elite,
sentences.zh: 那种深刻的英格兰精神被掏空并即将丧失，而地方特色即将被这种精英理念彻底粉碎的想法，

sentences.en: a sort of plutocratic elite.
sentences.zh: 一种财阀精英。

sentences.en: But also, I mean, there was a match when Chelsea played Newcastle just after Abramovich had been sanctioned.
sentences.zh: 而且，我的意思是，在阿布拉莫维奇受到制裁后，切尔西对阵纽卡斯尔的那场比赛，

sentences.en: And Johnson was about to fly out to Saudi Arabia to beg him for more oil at the same time as, you know, 81 people had been executed in Saudi Arabia.
sentences.zh: 当时约翰逊正准备飞往沙特阿拉伯乞求更多的石油，而与此同时，你知道，沙特阿拉伯有81人被处决。

sentences.en: And the sense that, you know, these two great historic teams with their devoted fan bases were both the toys of these kind of terrible people was, I thought,
sentences.zh: 那种感觉，你知道，这两支拥有忠实球迷群的伟大历史球队，竟然都成了这些可怕之人的玩具，我认为，

sentences.en: a kind of quite sobering moment.
sentences.zh: 是一个相当令人清醒的时刻。

sentences.en: I think so, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我也这么认为，汤姆。

sentences.en: I think, I mean, the clubs, certainly the highest level of the Premier League, the Premier League is kind of the one of the ultimate expressions of let it rip, rapacious,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，俱乐部，当然是英超联赛的最高水平，英超联赛是那种放任自流、贪婪的、

sentences.en: free market globalizations.
sentences.zh: 自由市场全球化的终极表现之一。

sentences.en: But the clubs themselves are kind of vessels of continuity through time.
sentences.zh: 但俱乐部本身是跨越时间的连续性的载体。

sentences.en: They embody traditions.
sentences.zh: 它们体现了传统。

sentences.en: And that's the appeal, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这就是吸引力所在，不是吗？

sentences.en: That's the appeal.
sentences.zh: 这就是吸引力所在。

sentences.en: You know, that's a huge appeal for, you know, so that I would guess the Premier League is one of the things for which England is best known today around the world.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这有巨大的吸引力，所以我猜英超联赛是当今世界最广为人知的英格兰事物之一。

sentences.en: I mean, everyone in China knows Manchester United and Liverpool.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，中国每个人都知道曼联和利物浦。

sentences.en: But that's also why the national team matters, because it's separate from the clubs.
sentences.zh: 但这也是国家队重要的原因，因为它独立于俱乐部之外。

sentences.en: You know, it's not owned by a golf autocrat or a Russian, what are they called, oligarchs.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它不是由某个高尔夫独裁者或俄罗斯人——他们叫什么来着，寡头——所拥有的。

sentences.en: Hobsbawm, Eric Hobsbawm, the historian, said something I like.
sentences.zh: 霍布斯鲍姆，埃里克·霍布斯鲍姆，那位历史学家，说过一些我喜欢的话。

sentences.en: He said, the imagined community of millions seems more real as a team of 11 named people.
sentences.zh: 他说，数百万人的想象共同体，作为一支由11个有名有姓的人组成的球队，似乎显得更加真实。

sentences.en: And you see that too in cricket, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你在板球运动中也能看到这一点。

sentences.en: I mean, you're a great cricket fan.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你是一位伟大的板球迷。

sentences.en: Well, OK, so what, but Jason, what I'd say about that is that, I mean, pretty much every country has a football team, has a national football team.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那又怎样，但杰森，我想说的是，几乎每个国家都有足球队，都有国家足球队。

sentences.en: I mean, you could say that about Italy, you could say it about Germany, you could say it about Spain, you could say it about Brazil.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可以对意大利这么说，对德国这么说，对西班牙这么说，对巴西这么说。

sentences.en: I mean, you could say that country's across the world.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可以对世界各地的国家这么说。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But is there anything particularly English about supporting your national team?
sentences.zh: 但支持你的国家队有什么特别的英格兰特色吗？

sentences.en: No, but what we're talking about is how the England team is an expression of the changing English nation.
sentences.zh: 没有，但我们谈论的是英格兰队如何成为不断变化的英格兰民族的一种表达。

sentences.en: And it's a contested identity.
sentences.zh: 这是一种有争议的身份认同。

sentences.en: I think we wouldn't be having this conversation if we didn't believe it's a contested identity.
sentences.zh: 我想如果我们不相信这是一种有争议的身份认同，我们就不会进行这场对话了。

sentences.en: And football has been one of the, the English football national team has been one of the means by which we have grappled with this contested identity.
sentences.zh: 足球一直是，英格兰国家足球队一直是我们就这种有争议的身份认同进行抗争的手段之一。

sentences.en: And also begun to understand how the nation has changed and who the, who the English are today.
sentences.zh: 也开始理解这个国家是如何改变的，以及今天的英格兰人究竟是谁。

sentences.en: You're right, Tom, when you said at the beginning, some of my black friends, particularly in the 80s and 90s, were very uncomfortable about blackness and Englishness.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你说得对，你在开头时说，我的一些黑人朋友，特别是在80年代和90年代，对黑人身份和英格兰身份感到非常不自在。

sentences.en: And they would, they would describe themselves as black British, first and foremoSt.
sentences.zh: 他们会首先把自己描述为“黑人英国人”。

sentences.en: That was a distinct identity for them.
sentences.zh: 这对他们来说是一种独特的身份。

sentences.en: But what we've seen in recent times, delightfully, in my view, is, is a, is a black English identity developing.
sentences.zh: 但近年来我们所看到的，在我看来令人欣喜的是，一种黑人英格兰人的身份正在形成。

sentences.en: And I think that's all for, all for the good.
sentences.zh: 我认为这完全是件好事。

sentences.en: And I will, and I welcome it.
sentences.zh: 我对此表示欢迎。

sentences.en: Can I change the focus a little bit?
sentences.zh: 我可以稍微转换一下焦点吗？

sentences.en: So we started with Orwell, who, I mean, he's, he's, he's politically so hard to pin down, but let's just say for the sake of argument, at least initially a man of the left,
sentences.zh: 我们从奥威尔开始，我的意思是，他在政治上很难被定义，但我们姑且不论，至少最初他是一个左翼人士，

sentences.en: you edit a magazine that's traditionally been seen as left of center magazine.
sentences.zh: 你编辑的一本杂志传统上被视为左翼杂志。

sentences.en: And for as long as you have edited it, I think you have run stories.
sentences.zh: 而且在你担任编辑的这段时间里，我想你刊登过很多报道。

sentences.en: I mean, I've written, I wrote one of them myself about the left and Englishness and the problem with Englishness about the knee.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我自己就写过一篇关于左翼和英格兰精神，以及关于下跪行为的英格兰精神问题的文章。

sentences.en: I mean, people were arguing about this with the so-called blue labor moment at the beginning of the 2010s.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，人们在2010年代初围绕所谓的“蓝色工党”时刻争论过这个问题。

sentences.en: And you talk in the book about the sort of the death of a kind of labor England.
sentences.zh: 你在书中谈到了某种工党英格兰的消亡。

sentences.en: Do you think there is a kind of way back for the left in England and kind of with England, I suppose?
sentences.zh: 你认为英格兰的左翼还有回归的可能吗，我想，和英格兰一起？

sentences.en: Or because of course, as we said earlier, there are so many people on the left for whom the very idea of England and Englishness is, is unsettling and they don't like it.
sentences.zh: 或者因为当然，正如我们之前所说，左翼中有许多人对英格兰和英格兰精神的理念感到不安，他们不喜欢它。

sentences.en: So how do they get that back?
sentences.zh: 那么他们该如何找回它呢？

sentences.en: Yes, I think, I think it's a huge, it's a huge challenge for the left and particularly for the Labour Party, because the Labour Party was once so strong in Scotland, where,
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这对左翼，特别是对工党来说是一个巨大的挑战，因为工党曾经在苏格兰非常强大，在那里，

sentences.en: where indeed it was hegemonic.
sentences.zh: 它确实占据了霸权地位。

sentences.en: In the 2015 general election, Ed Miliband went into that election with 41 of the 59 Scottish seats at Westminster and came out of it with one, the S&P 156.
sentences.zh: 在2015年大选中，埃德·米利班德带着威斯敏斯特59个苏格兰席位中的41个进入选举，结果只剩下一个，苏格兰民族党赢得了56个。

sentences.en: I think from which there is no return for labor.
sentences.zh: 我认为工党从此再无翻身之日。

sentences.en: I think the progressives in Scotland, many of them are now nationalists and they've embraced the S&P, not least because the S&P have power and are in control of the money.
sentences.zh: 我认为苏格兰的进步人士，他们中的许多人现在是民族主义者，他们拥抱了苏格兰民族党，不仅因为苏格兰民族党拥有权力并控制着资金。

sentences.en: And all the institutions that are built around power and government are now with the nationalists.
sentences.zh: 而且所有围绕权力和政府建立的机构现在都站在民族主义者一边。

sentences.en: So, you know, what does Labour have to do?
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，工党必须做什么？

sentences.en: Labour has to, Labour has to, Labour has, if Labour is ever to win a majority, again, in the United Kingdom, it has to start winning in England.
sentences.zh: 工党必须，工党必须，工党如果想在英国再次赢得多数席位，就必须开始在英格兰获胜。

sentences.en: But what we saw at the last general election in particular was a huge rejection of the Labour Party in many of its traditional heartlands, in the north of England, in the Midlands.
sentences.zh: 但我们在上次大选中特别看到的是，工党在英格兰北部、中部等许多传统腹地遭到了巨大的拒绝。

sentences.en: You know, it can't, it loses in Essex, where I'm from.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它在埃塞克斯也输了，我就是那里人。

sentences.en: I don't think there's a single Labour constituency in Essex.
sentences.zh: 我认为埃塞克斯没有一个工党选区。

sentences.en: But if it's ever to start winning again, it has to reconnect with many of its traditional voters, those who want, you know, Labour,
sentences.zh: 但如果它想再次开始获胜，它必须与许多传统选民重新建立联系，那些想要，你知道，工党，

sentences.en: the Labour Party was founded to represent the Labour interest, organised Labour.
sentences.zh: 工党成立的初衷是代表劳工利益，有组织的劳工。

sentences.en: But it was always an uneasy coalition between organised Labour and what you might say the Fabian or Hampstead intellectual.
sentences.zh: 但它一直是有组织劳工与你可能所说的费边社或汉普斯特德知识分子之间不安的联盟。

sentences.en: The prune juice drinkers.
sentences.zh: 那些喝西梅汁的人。

sentences.en: Yes, yes, whatever you call, whatever you call those people, they founded the New Statesman in 1913.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的，无论你叫什么，无论你叫那些人什么，他们在1913年创办了《新政治家》杂志。

sentences.en: But that coalition, if not definitively broken, is fractured into multiple pieces.
sentences.zh: 但那个联盟，如果不是彻底破裂，也已经碎片化了。

sentences.en: And Labour is very strong in the cities, in London, in Manchester, in Liverpool, in Cambridge, in Oxford.
sentences.zh: 工党在城市中非常强大，在伦敦、曼彻斯特、利物浦、剑桥、牛津。

sentences.en: But it's strong among the educated, urban middle class, and very weak everywhere else.
sentences.zh: 但在受过教育的城市中产阶级中很强大，而在其他任何地方都很弱。

sentences.en: And that's not a stable coalition to win.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个能赢得选举的稳定联盟。

sentences.en: I mean, one of the things that does strike me about England, and I think you could say Britain more generally, over the past 10 years,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，过去10年来，有一件事确实让我对英格兰，我想你也可以更广泛地说是英国，印象深刻，

sentences.en: I mean, it's been clearly been a very, very convulsive, turbulent, exhausting period, and very upsetting for a broad range of people for all different kinds of reasons.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这显然是一个非常、非常痉挛、动荡、令人筋疲力尽的时期，由于各种各样的原因，让广大民众感到非常不安。

sentences.en: But I think you could also say that it's been an affirmation of the commitment of England and Britain, perhaps more generally, to principles of democracy.
sentences.zh: 但我认为你也可以说，这肯定了英格兰和英国，或许更广泛地说，对民主原则的承诺。

sentences.en: Because what we've seen is how turbulent democracy can be.
sentences.zh: 因为我们所看到的是民主可以有多么动荡。

sentences.en: We have had two existential referenduMs.
sentences.zh: 我们举行了两次存在主义公投。

sentences.en: We've had one on the very makeup of the country that we live in.
sentences.zh: 我们举行了一次关于我们所居住国家的构成本身的公投。

sentences.en: And we've had another on the most significant foreign affairs context within which Britain had operated.
sentences.zh: 我们还举行了另一次关于英国运作的最重要的外交事务背景的公投。

sentences.en: And we have had referendums on both, and we have abided by the results on both.
sentences.zh: 我们对这两者都进行了公投，并且我们都遵守了结果。

sentences.en: And also, however much criticism one might level at our parliamentary system, and first past the post, it has facilitated the articulation of some quite kind of radical positions.
sentences.zh: 而且，无论人们对我们的议会制度和“胜者全得”选举制有多少批评，它确实促进了一些相当激进立场的表达。

sentences.en: So whether that's the SNP in Scotland, whether that is Nigel Farage, who you have cited as perhaps the most influential political figure in recent history,
sentences.zh: 所以，无论是苏格兰的苏格兰民族党（SNP），还是你所提到的、或许是近代史上最具影响力的政治人物奈杰尔·法拉奇，

sentences.en: even though he's never been an MP, or Corbyn, and giving a voice to the further reaches of the Labour Party on the left.
sentences.zh: 尽管他从未担任过议员，又或是科尔宾，他们都为工党左翼的边缘声音提供了表达渠道。

sentences.en: So couldn't you say that, in a sense, although things may look bleak for Labour, there's still all to play for?
sentences.zh: 那么你是否可以认为，从某种意义上说，尽管工党的前景看起来很黯淡，但一切仍有变数？

sentences.en: Because at the moment, we're on such a rollercoaster, we don't quite know where we're going to get to.
sentences.zh: 因为目前我们正处于过山车般的动荡中，我们并不完全确定最终会走向何方。

sentences.en: Yes, I think all of that.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想确实如此。

sentences.en: I think expect the unexpected.
sentences.zh: 我认为要做好迎接意外的准备。

sentences.en: I think the reason Brexit was such a shock for the cognitive elite, to use a David Goodhart phrase,
sentences.zh: 我认为，用大卫·古德哈特的话来说，英国脱欧之所以让“认知精英”感到如此震惊，

sentences.en: was because it was so unexpected.
sentences.zh: 是因为它太出人意料了。

sentences.en: Orwell, in the essay we've cited throughout this podcast, uses a phrase about the elites receiving a tug from below when ordinary people are heard.
sentences.zh: 奥威尔在我们整个播客中引用的那篇文章里，用了一个短语来形容精英阶层：当普通民众发出声音时，他们会感到来自底层的拉扯。

sentences.en: And they were certainly heard loud and clear during that Brexit referendum.
sentences.zh: 在英国脱欧公投期间，他们的声音确实被清晰地听到了。

sentences.en: And it was such a shock, you know, it swept David Cameron out of power, it brought Boris Johnson ultimately to 10 Downing Street, and it was an exercise in democracy.
sentences.zh: 这太令人震惊了，你知道，它让大卫·卡梅伦下台，最终将鲍里斯·约翰逊送进了唐宁街10号，这是一次民主的实践。

sentences.en: Am I being overly nationalist, if I say that actually, other European Union countries had referendums on similar issues,
sentences.zh: 如果我说其他欧盟国家在类似问题上也举行过公投，而当选民投出“错误”的结果时，他们被告知重新投票，我是不是太民族主义了？

sentences.en: and when the electorate delivered the wrong result, they were told to go and vote again?
sentences.zh: 他们确实被告知重新投票，这不正是许多狂热的留欧派所希望的吗？

sentences.en: They were told to go and vote again, indeed, which was what a lot of ardent Remainers wanted, didn't they?
sentences.zh: 他们希望选民重新考虑，他们想要第二次公投。

sentences.en: They wanted the electorate to think again, and they wanted the second referendum.
sentences.zh: 但正如大卫·卡梅伦所做的那样，通过单一的二元公投来决定英国外交政策中如此重要、根本的部分，即是否留在欧盟，这是一种非凡的冒险行为，不是吗？

sentences.en: But to decide such an important, fundamental part of British foreign policy, in other words, membership of the European Union,
sentences.zh: 嗯，确实是，确实是。但话说回来，就像苏格兰公投一样，从某种意义上说，这些都是各政党在大选中做出的承诺。

sentences.en: on a single binary plebiscite, as David Cameron did, was an extraordinary exercise in risk-taking, wasn't it?
sentences.zh: 因此，你可以说，这表明英国的民主制度正在发挥作用，因为你知道，法拉奇显然代表了广大选民的呼声，
